headline: Celtics look ready for business after crushing Hornets in home debut
morning_brew: Wednesday night was about as smooth as it gets at the Garden, with the C's putting a real hurting on the Charlotte Hornets to the tune of a twenty-one-point win. After the way things ended last spring, it was a massive relief to see the squad come out with that kind of energy and just dismantle an opponent from the jump. The ball movement was crisp, the defense was suffocating, and for one night at least, we didn't have to sweat out a single possession like I'm watching a horror movie through my fingers. It is only one win, but that is the kind of clean, efficient basketball that reminds you why we're always in the conversation.

Jayson Tatum looked like a man on a mission, leading the charge with nineteen points and filling up the stat sheet while Neemias Queta and Luka Garza provided a huge spark off the bench. It was absolute magic to watch the second unit take over and keep the lead ballooning late in the game, especially with how active they were on the glass and in the passing lanes. Payton Pritchard was dealing all night long, picking up eleven assists and basically orchestrating the offense like he had the whole playbook memorized before he even checked in. If our bench keeps playing with that kind of fire, the rest of the league is gonna have a long, miserable season trying to keep up with us.

Looking ahead, we've got a few days to catch our breath before we hit the road for Detroit next Tuesday. It is a nice stretch of time to let the guys stay in the rhythm of practice while we see how the rest of the league shakes out in these final preseason looks. I am not gonna get ahead of myself and start talking about another banner, but if we keep playing like we did on Wednesday, this could be a hell of a year to be a fan in the Hub. For now, I am just happy we finally got a game that didn't require me to keep a bottle of antacids on the coffee table.

news_digest.headline: What NBA preseason has revealed about the Lakers, 76ers, Celtics and every team
news_digest.dans_take: All these national writers can analyze the preseason until they're blue in the face, but the C's look like they're playing a different sport.
